text:
joni: FYI hit a duplicate-create bug when our python client retried a POST after a backend 504. No Idempotency-Key so create happened twice.
kevin: ouch. which sdk version and sync/async?
joni: py-sdk 0.9.3, sync. We had a short request timeout, server returned 504 while body upload was in flight; client retried and backend returned 201.
laura: is this a transport-level stream replay or higher-level middleware retry?
joni: from logs it looks like the retry middleware retried the whole request; the sync transport buffered the body for small JSON, so it replayed fine, leading to duplicate.
sam: historically we left idempotency to customers. A safe hardening is to auto-generate an Idempotency-Key when retrying POSTs, but that changes semantics. Maybe opt-in via client config with a warning by default.
kevin: short-term mitigation: reduce retry attempts on POST and add a runtime warning if POST+retries+no idempotency key. Longer term: idempotency middleware that emits UUID v4 when permitted.
laura: async client has a separate bug where generator bodies can't be rewound; I'll take that. Plan: buffer async bodies only if content-length <= 512KB; otherwise mark non-replayable and surface a clear error suggesting to set Idempotency-Key or disable retries.
joni: created minimal repro: https://git.internal/repros/py-post-replay (internal)
sam: also need to document behavior difference in typing: AsyncClient signature needs clearer docs on retry and replay limitations.
kevin: ensure backoff uses decorrelated jitter and not immediate retries for 5xx. Differentiate between idempotent methods and POSTs.
laura: will add unit tests for replayable bodies: sync vs async, small JSON, file stream, generator, explicit id key present.
devex-bot: Created ticket DE-4930: "py-sdk: POST replay causing duplicate resource; async replay buffering + idempotency middleware" assigned to laura and sam.
joni: thanks — I'll alert the impacted customer and share the repro logs.
